proposal.summary: LearnPress WordPress plugin (versions before 4.1.5) allows authenticated users to upload an avatar image (JPG/PNG), crop it, and submit a POST request containing a user-supplied image name. The server renames the image to an MD5-derived name based on that supplied name, enabling an attacker to rename arbitrary image files which could disrupt site design.
proposal.cwe_quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file.

AV.quote: a "POST" request that contains user supplied name of the image is sent to the server for renaming and cropping of the image.

PR.quote: Users of the LearnPress WordPress plugin before 4.1.5 can upload an image as a profile avatar after the registration.

UI.quote: a "POST" request that contains user supplied name of the image is sent to the server for renaming and cropping of the image.

C.quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file. By doing this, they could destroy the design of the web site.

A.quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file. By doing this, they could destroy the design of the web site.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Attempt to reproduce the issue on a test instance with an unprivileged user account: register or log in, upload a JPG/PNG avatar, submit a crafted POST with a chosen filename, and observe whether arbitrary existing image files are renamed. Collect the exact request/response and file-system effects for patching and to create a proof-of-concept.

evidence_quotes.claim: Affected versions / capability to upload after registration
evidence_quotes.quote: Users of the LearnPress WordPress plugin before 4.1.5 can upload an image as a profile avatar after the registration.

evidence_quotes.claim: Flow: crop and save triggers POST with user-supplied name
evidence_quotes.quote: After this process the user crops and saves the image. Then a "POST" request that contains user supplied name of the image is sent to the server for renaming and cropping of the image.

evidence_quotes.claim: Server changes name to MD5 value
evidence_quotes.quote: As a result of this request, the name of the user-supplied image is changed with a MD5 value.
This process can be conducted only when type of the image is JPG or PNG.

evidence_quotes.claim: Impact: rename arbitrary image file and break design
evidence_quotes.quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file. By doing this, they could destroy the design of the web site.
